The Hagerstown is a classic cold-blast hurricane lantern, named for the town where it is assembled
and tested. It is the lantern on the porch of half the farmhouses in Washington County. A 12-ounce
tank gives about 20 hours of light on a trimmed wick, the globe lifts for lighting with the lever
on the side, and the whole lantern can be carried in the rain. It uses a standard #2 flat wick,
part W-78, and we stock the wicks in 5-packs. The galvanized finish is bare steel and will develop
a patina outdoors; the red and black are powder coated.

The Heritage No. 7 is the oil lamp we have made in one form or another since 1987, and the only
product in this catalogue that carries a 10-year warranty. The font is spun from solid brass and
polished by hand; the burner is nickel-plated brass; the chimney is borosilicate glass. It burns
Clearburn lamp oil only. Kerosene will work but smokes and smells, and it voids the Heritage
Promise. A full 14-ounce font gives about 30 hours of light. The chimney is part CH-7 and is the
only part that breaks in normal use; it is sold separately and ships in a padded box.

Compatible parts: chimney CH-7, #2 flat wick 5-pack W-78, Clearburn Lamp Oil LS-OIL1.

# About Lantern Supply Co.

Last updated: October 1, 2026
Owner: Priya Whitcomb-Nair

Lantern Supply Co. sells camping lanterns, oil lamps, fuel and parts from two showrooms in
Maryland and from the online store at lanternsupply.example. We make some of what we sell, we
repair everything we sell, and we have been doing both since 1987. This page is the short version
of who we are, for new employees and for customers who ask.

## The story

Marjorie and Dale Whitcomb opened the first store in 1987 in a former hardware shop at 412 East
Patrick Street in Frederick, Maryland, the same building we occupy today. Dale had repaired
pressure lanterns for the Boy Scouts for years and could not find a shop that would sell a decent
oil lamp or a spare mantle; Marjorie ran the books and the counter. The first product with our
name on it was the Heritage No. 7 brass oil lamp, which Dale designed and had made by a brass
spinner in Baltimore, and which we still sell with a 10-year warranty.

For the first ten years the business was lamps, wicks, fuel and repairs. In 2003 the company
assembled its first Hagerstown Kerosene Lantern in a rented bay in Hagerstown, and in 2009 it
sold its first LED lantern, the Firefly 100. The online store opened in 2011. The Annapolis
showroom opened in May 2014, and in 2016 the warehouse and Repair Center moved into the current
building at 1180 Downsville Pike in Hagerstown, with the loading dock at Dock B that every return
and repair comes through.

Firefly 220R USB-C port
A 220R that will not charge is usually the cable, then the port, then the pack, in that order.
Test with the bench cable (part C-15) before opening anything.
1. Open the base (three screws) and lift out the pack. Pack part is B-220R.
2. The port is part of the main board (PCB-220R); the board is replaced as a unit, $9.00
on a paid repair.
3. On refit, check the port cover seals; the 220R is IPX4 and the cover is part of that
rating.
4. Charge to full on the bench (about 3.5 hours) and check the power bank output with
the load tester: it should hold 5 V at 1 A for 10 minutes.

Heritage No. 7 (LS-H7)
The Heritage No. 7 is a solid brass oil lamp with a 10-year warranty, so treat every one as a
red tag unless the ticket says otherwise. It burns Clearburn lamp oil only. Faults are a
cracked chimney (part CH-7), a wick that will not wind, and tarnish that the customer wants
removed. Tarnish is not a defect, but we polish the lamp as a courtesy on any repair.
Chimney
1. Lift the chimney straight up out of the gallery. Do not twist it; the gallery prongs will
scratch the glass.
2. Fit the new CH-7 with the seam at the back, and check the four prongs hold it without
play.
Wick
1. The Heritage takes a 7/8-inch flat wick, part W-H7. Wind the old wick up and out.
2. Feed the new wick with the weave running lengthwise. Trim it level with the top of the
burner, then round the corners.
3. Soak it for 10 minutes in lamp oil before lighting.
Brass care
1. Polish with the brass polish in the Heritage drawer and a soft cloth, in straight strokes.
2. Never use the polish on the burner threads; wipe them with a dry cloth only.
3. A customer who asks how to keep the lamp bright is told: a soft cloth after each use,
polish twice a year, and no lacquer.

Beacon 400 (LS-400), discontinued
The Beacon 400 was discontinued in March 2025. We stock its parts until March 2028 and
repair it on yellow and red tags until then. The procedure is the same as the Beacon 600's;
the globe is part G-400 and the gasket G-400G. There is no red night mode to test.
Parts bins
Parts are in the numbered bins along the north wall. The bin number is on the ticket when
the part is picked. Catalogue prices apply on paid repairs.

| Warranty | 2 years (battery 1 year) |

The Porchlight is a solar lantern for a porch, a fence post or a dock. The panel in the lid
charges the battery through the day and a light sensor turns the lantern on at dusk and off at
dawn. A full day of sun gives the full 8 hours; a cloudy day gives about half that. There is
nothing to fill, change or plug in. The bracket in the box mounts to a post or a wall, and the
lantern lifts off the bracket to be carried.

Compatible parts: hanging bracket BR-PS1.
